previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with rectal bleeding and abdominal pain radiating to the chest, in the context of chronic alcohol use, tobacco dependence, and known esophageal reflux. Evaluation confirmed guaiac-positive stool and anemia of chronic disease, with no infectious cause found on stool testing. Imaging from a recent admission showed findings consistent with alcoholic liver damage, esophageal thickening, and significant periportal lymphadenopathy. The patient was stabilized without intervention, and the bleeding subsided during the short stay. He was discharged with plans for gastroenterology follow-up, management of anemia, and referrals for alcohol and tobacco use counseling. Microscopic hematuria was incidentally noted but deemed non-urgent.
problems: Other and unspecified noninfectious gastroenteritis and colitis

Brief Hospital Course:
******* Patient left AMA**********

___ EtOH abuse with frequent admissions for abdominal pain and 
BRBPR presented with hematemesis and abdominal pain.

#Hematemasis: With history of alcohol abuse and patient came in 
intoxicated we felt his story was suggestive of ___ 
tear.  Ht 24 when admitted (baseline 30), was transfused on 
___ and Ht went up appropriately to 30. GI was consulted, EGD 
___ showed gastritis, they could not visualize bleed. EGD also 
showed grad I varices. Colonoscopy was also done which showed 
AVM which was clamped and internal hemhorroids grade 3. GI team 
felt the source of the bleed is likely ___ tear though 
was not seen on EGD. Pt had no hematemesis during hospital stay 
and his Ht remained stable 32. H pylori negative. Plan was for 
him to be discahged on omeprazole 40 BID and ferrous sulfate 
taken with vit C, however - despite a conversation and agreement 
between me and pt. on the day of planned discharge about the 
plan outlined here and that pt. would be discharged by 2pm after 
completion of all required paperwork and a review of d/c plan as 
written between pt. and his primary RN in the hospital (per 
routine), pt. eloped prior to the planned formal d/c against the 
advice and plan we agreed to in the am of the same day.

#SOB: Patient had episodes where he felt SOB when walking to the 
bathroom and had crackles on exam and mild ___ edema.  He never 
required nasal canula. At first we were concerned this may be 
cardiac related (he has a murmer) vs vol overload from 
cirrhosis. While here we had an echo done which showed mild 
symmetric LVH with normal global and regional biventricular 
systolic function. Aortic sclerosis without valvular stenosis. 
Borderline pulmonary hypertension. CXR on ___ showed no pulm 
edema. He was given 20 IV lasix which he responded well too. 
This SOB may also be related to his cirrhosis. We felt he would 
do well with a plan for 20 mg oral lasix daily, however the pt. 
eloped (see above) 

# Chest Pain/epigastric pain: During hospital admission pt 
complained of chest pain/epigastric pain. He had several EKGs 
all of which were unchanged compared to prior. Negative trop x3. 
We felt reassured this was not ACS. We felt abdominal pain was 
most likely related to ___ tear. EGD showed gastritis 
and it is also possible the pain is from that. Also on our 
differential was SBP. ___ did u/s to look for ascites to do a 
diagnostic tap however there was not enough fluid to tap. At one 
point during exam patient had positive carnetts sign which makes 
abdominal pain likely related to abdominal wall/muscles. While 
he was here we treated him with morphine 15mg PO about twice a 
day for pain. We feel that with time and PP-i his ___ 
tear will heal and he will feel better. Proposed plan was for 
follow up with new primary MD as well as hepatology here, but 
pt. eloped prior to formal discharge.

#Cirrhosis: Patient had no official diagnosis of cirrhosis 
before coming in. He had stable varices seen on EGD. RUQ U/S 
showed mild perihepatic ascites, focal gallbladder wall 
thickening, edema. Findings are likely due to underlying liver 
disease CT scan showed likely cirrhosis. Colonoscopy showed 
internal hemhorroids. We feel cirrhosis is likely related to 
alcohol. He was started on nadolol and dose was increased to 
60mg daily. He was also treated for SBP prophylactically because 
of GIB, given ceftriaxone 1g daily and was to be d/c'd on 
levofloxacin, for a total course of antibiotics for 1 wk. 

#HTN: SBP in the 150-160s had couple of readings in the 190s 
while in hospital and echo showed LVH likely from HTN.  We 
started him on lisinopril this admission,10 mg daily and 
increased lisinopril to 20.  We also started nadolol this 
admission.  

# Intoxication: Pt was admitted with alcohol intoxication. Per 
pt no history of withdrawal or seizures. Last drink was ___ 
before admission. Was given a bannana bag on day of admission, 
then given thiamine IV for 3 days. Initially he was on CIWA and 
on ___ hospital day CIWA was d/c'd because patient was not 
scoring. Social work was consulted and they discussed his issues 
___ housing.

# Lung Nodule: 1.2 cm nodular opacity projecting over the right 
mid lung was seen on CXR from ___.  This nodule was not seen 
on second CXR that was ordered on ___. On the second CXR 
radiologists interpreted film as RLL PNA, given clinical history 
of recent EGD, no fever, no white count, we felt that patient 
likely had pneumonitis and we did not feel he needed to be 
treated. Patient will need repeat CXR in about 4 weeks to follow 
up on the lung nodule.

#CXR showing possible RLL PNA: We had a CXR done do evaluate for 
pulm edema. It showed no pulm edema but showed a possible RLL 
PNA. We felt this was likely related to pneumonitis from EGD as 
patient had no fever, no cough, no white count. Regardless, plan 
to complete SBP prophylaxis with levofloxacin which will 
addtionally treat common (CAP)

It remains unclear how much of the plan will be able to be 
communicated to pt. and what he will comply with given his 
elopment.  After his elopement, attempts were made (many) to 
contact him to see the proposed treatment/discharge plan through 
to completion (see omr). 

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES - 
# Lung Nodule: 1.2 cm nodular opacity projecting over the right

#SOB: patient responded well to IV lasix 20 while in the
